reviews.rationale: Sequential Q2-to-Q3 comparison of selected SEC rows shows a mixed picture rather than a clean confirmation. Top-line revenue increased, but total costs and expenses increased by more, so GAAP operating income declined; the cost build was concentrated in transaction expenses, marketing, technology development and customer support, partly offset by lower general and administrative expense. Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA also declined, so the operating softness is visible on both the GAAP and the company-defined non-GAAP basis, and the two do not diverge in direction. GAAP net income, pretax income and diluted EPS nevertheless rose, but the source-audited bridge attributes the pretax improvement to a swing in signed other income plus a smaller interest expense drag, not to operations; the non-GAAP other-expense addback moves in the opposite direction by the same amount, which is consistent with the same non-operating item being excluded from adjusted EBITDA. Income tax expense rose, so the net income improvement is not a tax effect. Because the thesis is a source-bounded baseline with no valuation, catalyst or invalidation conditions and no stated expectation for margin direction, the evidence does not confirm or refute a specific claim; it establishes that the operating trajectory and the headline earnings trajectory diverged. That divergence, plus the absence of segment, volume/pricing, guidance, backlog or cash-flow evidence in this extract, warrants a needs_review decision that preserves status and conviction and blocks downstream decisions pending a fuller filing review. No causal driver is asserted: the signed identities are arithmetic, and the extract contains no source-explicit statement linking any cost line to the margin change.
